Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which competition or event did Frances Marie Burke win?

Nicosia, Cyprus - In a stunning upset, American model Frances Marie Burke was crowned the winner of the coveted Miss Cyprus beauty contest, held at the luxurious Four Seasons Hotel in Nicosia on Saturday evening. "I'm completely overwhelmed and humbled by this incredible honor," Burke said in an exclusive interview with our publication, beaming with pride. Burke, who has modeled for top designers and appeared on the covers of numerous fashion magazines, wowed the judges with her stunning looks, impeccable style, and impressive answers to the panel's questions. "Frances was a standout from the very beginning," said Maria Georgiou, a member of the judging panel and renowned fashion designer. "Her confidence, charisma, and natural beauty shone through in every aspect of the competition. She truly embodies the spirit of Miss Cyprus." The competition, now in its 20th year, attracted a record number of applicants from around the globe. The contestants were put through a rigorous series of challenges, including a swimsuit round, evening gown segment, and a question-and-answer session. According to pageant organizers, this year's event saw a significant increase in viewership, with over 1 million people tuning in to watch the live broadcast. "Frances's win is a testament to the growing global appeal of the Miss Cyprus pageant," said Andreas Christodoulou, president of the Miss Cyprus Organization. "We're thrilled to have her as our new ambassador, and we're confident she'll do an outstanding job representing Cyprus on the international stage." As the new Miss Cyprus, Burke will embark on a year-long reign, during which she will participate in various charity events, fashion shows, and promotional activities. She will also represent Cyprus at the upcoming Miss World pageant in December. When asked about her plans for her reign, Burke said, "I'm excited to use my platform to make a positive impact on the lives of others.
Document 2: Title: The Crowning Glory: Frances Marie Burke's Triumph at Miss America

It was a chilly winter evening in February 1940 when the lights of the Warner Theatre in Atlantic City, New Jersey, shone bright, illuminating the stage for the 14th annual Miss America competition. Among the 42 contestants vying for the coveted title was a stunning 20-year-old from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania - Frances Marie Burke. Little did anyone know that this poised and charming young woman would soon make history, etching her name in the annals of American pageantry. Frances, a model by profession, had already gained recognition in the fashion world, gracing the covers of prominent magazines and strutting down catwalks with ease. Her experience in the industry had honed her confidence, and she was determined to bring home the Miss America crown. As the competition unfolded, Frances impressed the judges with her striking features, captivating stage presence, and impressive talent - a flawless rendition of the opera song "Caro Nome" from Verdi's Rigoletto. Her poise and elegance during the evening gown segment left the audience in awe, and her thoughtful responses to the judges' questions showcased her intelligence and wit. On February 10, 1940, the moment of truth arrived. The emcee, Bob Russell, announced the top five finalists, and Frances Marie Burke's name was among them. The tension was palpable as the judges deliberated, and finally, the results were in. With a beaming smile, Bob Russell declared, "And the new Miss America is... Frances Marie Burke!" The audience erupted in applause as Frances, resplendent in her evening gown, was crowned by the outgoing titleholder, Patricia Donnelly. The Philadelphia Inquirer reported, "Miss Burke's victory was a popular one, and she was mobbed by her fellow contestants and friends after the announcement." (1)

Frances's triumph was not limited to the stage alone. Her win marked a significant milestone in the history of the Miss America organization. She was the first contestant from Pennsylvania to claim the title, paving the way for future generations of Keystone State beauties. (2)

In the aftermath of her victory, Frances embarked on a whirlwind tour, traveling across the United States, and participating in various charity events, parades, and public appearances.
